s: Token bucket, sliding window, API quotas, DDoS protection
d: Rate limiting protects your API from abuse, ensures fair usage, and prevents DDoS attacks. Understanding algorithms (token bucket, sliding window), implementation layers (application, gateway, CDN), and quota management is critical for production APIs.
c: Rate limiting at different layers (app, gateway, CDN)
IP-based vs user-based vs API-key-based limiting

p: Rate Limiting restricts the number of requests a client (IP or User) can make to an API within a specific time window. It prevents DDoS attacks, brute forcing, and resource exhaustion.
1. Token Bucket: Tokens are added to a bucket at a fixed rate. Requests consume tokens.
2. Fixed Window: Max X requests per minute. Resets at top of minute.
3. Sliding Window: More accurate windowing based on precise timestamps.

// Express Rate Limit Middleware
const limiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes
  max: 100, // Limit each IP to 100 requests per windowMs
  message: "Too many requests, please try again later."
});
app.use('/api/', limiter);

Token Bucket Algorithm:
Bucket Capacity: 5 tokens. Refill rate: 1 token/sec.
Request 1 -> Takes token (4 left) -> OK
Request 2-5 -> Takes tokens (0 left) -> OK
Request 6 -> Bucket empty -> 429 TOO MANY REQUESTS
